{
  "summary": "Expands compressed IPv6 addresses sent to SOCKS5 proxies by writing out all eight groups instead of using `::`. This avoids an upstream Tor bug where `<name>:<port>` is parsed as a valid IPv6 address by Tor exit relays, which causes them to fail to detect the port and drop the connection.",
  "problem": "Nodes routing outbound traffic through a Tor proxy fail to connect to IPv6 peers whose addresses contain an inner `::`. Tor relays construct relay cells as `<name>:<port>`, causing the exit relay to absorb the port into the compressed IPv6 address as an eighth group and terminate the stream with a \"general failure\" error. Roughly 20% of addrman addresses and 29% of DNS seed IPv6 answers suffer from this silent connection failure.",

result.summary: Expands compressed IPv6 addresses sent to SOCKS5 proxies by writing out all eight groups instead of using `::`. This avoids an upstream Tor bug where `<name>:<port>` is parsed as a valid IPv6 address by Tor exit relays, which causes them to fail to detect the port and drop the connection.
result.problem: Nodes routing outbound traffic through a Tor proxy fail to connect to IPv6 peers whose addresses contain an inner `::`. Tor relays construct relay cells as `<name>:<port>`, causing the exit relay to absorb the port into the compressed IPv6 address as an eighth group and terminate the stream with a "general failure" error. Roughly 20% of addrman addresses and 29% of DNS seed IPv6 answers suffer from this silent connection failure.
evidence: Author tested against tor 0.4.9.13 on mainnet: master failed to connect to four seed-provided peers with inner-`::` addresses (30 "general failure" errors), whereas the PR connected and completed handshakes with all four.
Upstream Tor bug report at https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/core/tor/-/issues/32314 confirms the exit relay parser issue with compressed IPv6 addresses.
Author notes that "About 20% of the IPv6 addresses in a gossip-filled addrman, and 29% of current IPv6 DNS seed answers, have an inner `::`."
result.scope_notes: Diff is small (+80/-3) and includes unit test coverage in `netbase_tests` and functional test updates in `feature_proxy.py`.
result.card: Expands compressed IPv6 addresses into full eight-group notation when passing them to SOCKS5 proxies. Nodes using Tor as a general proxy cannot establish outbound connections to IPv6 peers containing an inner `::` because Tor exit relays mistake the appended port for an address group and terminate the connection. This bug drops connections to roughly 20-30% of reachable IPv6 peers on mainnet. Author verified on mainnet against tor 0.4.9.13 that connections failing on master succeed with this change.

risk.why: Incorrect string formatting of SOCKS5 target addresses could break outbound connections through Tor and other SOCKS5 proxies.
